hero.title: A Dutch virtual number for SMS verification
intro: If you've ever watched a product demo of phone verification, odds are you've seen a +31 6 number on screen — Dutch mobiles are something of a stock example in the industry. That familiarity works in your favor: forms everywhere know exactly what a Netherlands mobile looks like.

SMS Code gives you a real Dutch mobile number in one tap. Enter it when Telegram, WhatsApp, Google or another supported service asks for a phone, and the SMS with your code appears in the app usually within seconds.

whyCountry.title: Why choose a Dutch number?
body: The Netherlands is a compact, highly connected EU market, and a +31 number is a reliable European default — accepted by messengers like Telegram, WhatsApp and Signal, by community platforms like Discord, and by Google alike. When you don't need a specific country, you need a country that never causes problems, and Dutch numbers rarely do.

Every Dutch mobile follows one pattern: +31, then 6, then eight digits. No competing prefixes, no regional variants — a single unambiguous format that international forms parse on the first try, which keeps the verification step as boring as it should be.

tips.title: Mobile always means 6
tips.body: In the Netherlands the 6 after +31 is what marks a mobile — other leading digits are landlines and won't receive texts. Numbers from SMS Code are mobiles by definition, so the 6 is already in place.

tips.title: Zero out, plus in
tips.body: Written domestically the number starts 06; internationally the zero drops and +31 takes its place. If a form complains, check you haven't pasted the domestic 06 form into an international field.

tips.title: Second try is free if the first fails
tips.body: When a code doesn't arrive within the activation window, cancel it in the app — nothing is charged for unreceived activations — and take a new Dutch number for the retry.

faqs.q: Is it a real Dutch mobile number?
faqs.a: Yes — a number on a real carrier network in the standard +31 6 mobile range. To the service verifying you, it's indistinguishable from any resident's phone.

faqs.q: What are Dutch numbers a good fit for?
faqs.a: Messengers and everyday accounts above all — Telegram, WhatsApp, Signal, Discord and Google are common pairings — plus any service that simply wants a solid EU mobile.

faqs.q: Can I receive the SMS without being in the Netherlands?
faqs.a: Yes. The number lives inside the SMS Code app, so your physical location and your own SIM card are beside the point — the code shows up in the app wherever you are.

faqs.q: How do I pay for an activation?
faqs.a: From a one-time coin pack, per activation — no subscription running in the background. Activations that never receive an SMS cancel free, so failed attempts don't eat into your balance.

faqs.q: Should I keep anything tied to this number long-term?
faqs.a: No — treat it as the key that opens the door. Once the account exists, attach a recovery email and authenticator-app 2FA so future logins and recoveries never depend on the rented number.
